messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

Brackets are placeholders. Fill in your own details.

---

**Subject: [Service] is moving to [new platform] in [Q1 2027]**

Hi [name],

On [date], [Service] switches over to [new platform]. Here's the heads-up so it doesn't land on you cold.

The reason: [current platform can't do X]. [New platform] gets us [concrete thing: faster restores, regional hosting, a real API].

**Changes on your side**

- Sign in at [new URL]. The old address forwards there until [date].
- API calls go to [new base]. Old endpoints answer until [date] and return 410 after that.
- [Feature X] works differently now: [one sentence].

**Staying put**

Data, account history, billing date, existing integration credentials. All of it comes with us. No exports, no re-uploads.

**Cutover window**

[Date], [time range] [timezone]. The service goes read-only for roughly [N minutes/hours]. Watch [status page] for live updates.

**Your to-do list**

Empty, with one exception: if [old URL] is hardcoded in your setup, change it before [date]. Customers on [legacy plan] or running [SDK below vX] do need a manual step, so reply here and we'll sort it out together.

Reminders go out two weeks ahead and again the night before. Anything breaks after the switch, [support channel] gets to us fastest. We're doubling coverage there for the first fortnight.

[Name]
[Title], [Company]

---

Settle two questions before this goes out. First, naming the old platform is usually a mistake. Second, if you can quote the read-only window as one number instead of a range, do. Ranges signal guesswork.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
**Subject: Ledger Sync moves to Northwind on 14 January 2027**

Hi Dana,

On 14 January 2027, Ledger Sync starts running on Northwind. I'm telling you now so the date doesn't land on you cold.

The reason: our present setup keeps backups in one region and a full restore takes most of a day. Northwind gives us EU or US hosting per account, restores in under an hour, and a documented API instead of the half-public one you've been working against.

**What changes**

- Sign in at app.ledgersync.com. The old address redirects there through 30 June 2027.
- API calls go to api.ledgersync.com/v2. The v1 endpoints answer until 31 March 2027, then return 410.
- Scheduled exports run on your account timezone rather than UTC. Check any report you time to a cutoff.

**What doesn't**

Your data, account history, billing date, and current API keys come across untouched. No exports, no re-uploads.

**Cutover**

14 January, 02:00 UTC. Ledger Sync goes read-only for 40 minutes. Live updates at status.ledgersync.com.

**What we need from you**

Almost nothing. If the old hostname is hardcoded anywhere, change it before 31 March. Two groups need a manual step: accounts on the 2019 Starter plan, and anyone on the Python SDK below 4.0. Reply here and we'll walk it through with you.

Reminders go out two weeks ahead and again the evening before. If something breaks after the switch, support@ledgersync.com reaches us fastest. We're running double cover there for the first two weeks.

Priya Raghunathan
Head of Platform, Ledger Sync

---

Two things worth deciding before you send your own version. Naming the platform you're leaving rarely earns its keep. And quote the read-only window as a single number if you can stand behind one, because a range reads as a guess.
